newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan to quit Wednesday - coalition MP.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan to quit Wednesday - coalition MP.

text.p: A top member of Turkey's junior coalition party said on Monday that Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan would resign this week in a power-sharing deal to end a row over Islamist activism.
"Erbakan will resign on Wednesday in line with the coalition protocol," Anatolian news agency quoted True Path Party deputy chairman Hasan Ekinci as saying.
Erbakan and Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, the True Path Party leader, earlier announced they would swap jobs by the end of this month and form a caretaker government to go for early elections.

But the planned power transfer and early polls would have to overcome the serious obstacles of presidential and parliamentary approval. The coalition now lacks a majority in the national assembly after a series of defections.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, has been under intense pressure in recent months in an anti-Islamist campaign, led by the secularist army. Ciller says she could ward off the army better than Erbakan if she were made prime minister.
Erbakan declined at a news conference on Monday to fix a date for the power handover despite persistent questions from journalists on when he would stand down.
